claim_a_text: Anchor boxes are a key and necessary component for efficient and accurate object detection, enabling multi-scale predictions and feature sharing.
claim_b_text: Anchor boxes are not necessary for object detection; an anchor-free, fully convolutional approach can achieve better accuracy and is simpler.
claim_a_quote: We introduce novel Region Proposal Networks (RPNs) that share convolutional layers with state-of-the-art object detection networks... Our design of anchors presents a novel scheme for addressing multiple scales (and aspect ratios).
claim_b_quote: We hope that the proposed FCOS framework can serve as a simple and strong alternative for many other instance-level tasks. ... we encourage the community to rethink the necessity of anchor boxes in object detection, which are currently considered as the de facto standard for detection.
rationale: ARTICLE_A advocates for anchor boxes as a core, efficient design for multi-scale detection, while ARTICLE_B argues anchor boxes are unnecessary and proposes a simpler, anchor-free paradigm that surpasses anchor-based methods.
